title: Scientists: Extraterrestrial life likely exists somewhere in the universe
site_name: BGNES: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

content:
Among astrobiologists, 86.6% said they “agree” or “strongly agree” that such life probably exists.

However vast you imagine the universe to be, it is almost certainly even larger. Our Milky Way galaxy is about 100,000 light-years across, with one light-year equal to approximately 6 trillion miles, HuffPost reported.

Some estimates suggest there may be between one and two billion galaxies in the universe. It is therefore perhaps unsurprising that scientists have long wondered whether we can truly be alone in such an immense expanse.

For some experts, our interstellar solitude seems so unlikely that the question has given rise to the so-called Fermi paradox. Given how statistically probable the existence of other life appears to be, it asks: where are all the aliens?

Humanity has been searching for extraterrestrial life only since around the 1960s, and the sheer vastness of the universe, which makes its existence seem so likely, may at the same time make encountering it almost impossible.

A study published in the journal Nature Astronomy shows that most scientists agree that life probably exists somewhere beyond Earth.

What does the study show?

The study included four surveys of scientists, including astrobiologists, biologists and physicists. The questions concerned the “likely existence of basic, complex and intelligent extraterrestrial life”.

The aim was to determine whether experts considered it likely that anything from bacteria and plants to conscious beings exists elsewhere.

Among astrobiologists, 86.6% said they “agree” or “strongly agree” that such life probably exists.

Around 12% took a neutral position, while only 2% expressed disagreement.

Among scientists who are not astrobiologists, positive responses were even higher - 88.4% believe that life probably exists somewhere.

What about intelligent aliens?

“Extraterrestrial life” does not necessarily mean thinking and communicating beings of the kind we usually imagine when we hear the word “aliens”. It could be something as simple as a single-celled organism.

The researchers therefore also asked scientists how likely they thought the existence of “complex” and “intelligent” forms of life was.

Among astrobiologists, 67.4% said they considered this likely, compared with 58.2% of the other scientists.

Only 10.2% of astrobiologists categorically rejected such a possibility.

The results, the study authors said, “provide a snapshot of opinion within the scientific community and reveal a significant degree of agreement that extraterrestrial life probably exists”. | BGNES
